item.title: Voyager 1 reaches one light-day distance from Earth
item.description: NASA's Voyager 1 reached a distance of approximately 16.1 billion miles (25.9 billion kilometers) from Earth on November 18, 2026 at 2:16 a.m. PST, equivalent to one light-day. It is the first human-made object to achieve this distance. Radio signals now take approximately 24 hours to reach Earth, making communication take nearly two days for a round trip. Voyager 1...

item.title: Extinct grasshoppers may have walked on water alongside dinosaurs
item.description: Nearly 100 million years ago, grasshoppers with long, spindly legs may have walked on water, much like today's water striders. This emerges from fossil insects beautifully preserved in amber. Their legs and feet display distinctive hairs and leaf-shaped protrusions that, according to researchers, helped maintain balance and glide across the water surface by exploiting surface tension. item.title: Volunteers rescue centuries-old letters with Cursive for a Cause project
item.description: Since cursive writing disappeared from American educational standards in 2010, the ability to read it has been at risk. At Bowling Green State University, AmeriCorps volunteers are fighting back with the project 'Cursive for a Cause'. item.title: Original Avengers cast dubs film in endangered Lakota language
item.description: In 2024, the actors from the original 'Avengers' film re-recorded their roles, this time in Lakota, a critically endangered Native American language. Only 2,000 people still speak the language, a decline of 66% in ten years. item.title: BeSeen machine helps homeless people around the clock
item.description: An Oklahoma-based non-profit, the BeHeard Movement, launched the BeSeen Machine: the world's first vending machine for homeless people operated entirely by virtual volunteers. item.description: On Turkey's Mediterranean coast, former fishers are working as marine rangers to protect fish stocks and their habitats. item.title: Sea urchins wear shells like little hats
item.description: Sea urchins have a habit of placing shells, stones and other bits of debris on their bodies, like a kind of hat. item.description: Faith Christian Academy on Yap, an island in Micronesia, now allows families to use coconuts to pay school tuition instead of cash. item.title: Wolbachia mosquitoes reduce virus infections in Brazil
item.description: In Belo Horizonte, Brazil, the release of mosquitoes infected with Wolbachia bacteria led to a 68.5% decline in dengue infections and 73.3% in chikungunya among schoolchildren. The four-year EVITA dengue trial tested a locally adapted wMel strain of Wolbachia that inhibits virus transmission by Aedes aegypti mosquitoes. item.title: Turning off radiators in empty rooms actually increases heating costs
item.description: Many people turn off radiators in guest rooms, home offices or utility rooms to save energy, but according to French agency ADEME, this backfires. Cold air is heavier and seeps under doors and through walls into heated rooms, causing them to cool faster. Radiators elsewhere must work harder, putting greater strain on the heating system.
